title: Modality-Balanced Collaborative Distillation for Multi-Modal Domain Generalization
publication_status_observed: arXiv:2511.20258v3 [cs.CV] 28 Jan 2026; venue header states 'AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence' (AAAI 2026)
main_claims: Directly applying EMA/weight averaging to multi-modal domain generalisation leads to modality imbalance: dominant modalities converge faster and skew the averaged parameters toward sharper, less generalisable minima.

MBCD—combining adaptive modality dropout, a gradient consistency constraint, and EMA-based collaborative distillation—retains EMA's flatness-inducing advantages while correcting for modality imbalance.
MBCD consistently outperforms existing MMDG methods on EPIC-Kitchens and HAC benchmarks while converging to flatter loss landscapes.
methodology: MBCD uses three components: (1) Adaptive modality dropout probabilistically suppresses over-dominant modalities based on confidence ratio; (2) A gradient consistency constraint aligns gradients of uni-modal and multi-modal losses via inner-product maximisation; (3) An EMA-based teacher provides cross-modal distillation via KL-divergence loss from the fused prediction. Loss landscape flatness is measured by perturbation-based loss increase. Experiments use EPIC-Kitchens and HAC with three modalities (video, audio, optical flow), comparing to ERM, RNA-Net, SimMMDG, MOOSA, and CMRF.
key_results: MBCD achieves average 67.58% accuracy on EPIC-Kitchens tri-modal multi-source DG, vs. 65.47% for CMRF (the next best) and 50.55% for ERM.
Flatness analysis (Fig. 3) shows MBCD consistently converges to flatter minima than all baselines including EMA and CMRF, demonstrating that modality-balanced training leads to flatter solutions.
Ablation shows EMA alone provides the largest single-component gain (+4.47% over ERM), with adaptive dropout, gradient consistency, and distillation each contributing additional improvements.
limitations: The method is specific to multi-modal domain generalisation; there is no analysis of uni-modal discriminative OOD settings.
Theoretical analysis is limited to a bias-variance decomposition argument; no formal flatness guarantees are derived.
Experiments use only two multi-modal benchmarks; generalisation to other MMDG settings is not evaluated.
relevance_to_rq: This paper is peripheral to the RQ. It uses weight averaging for flatness in a multi-modal DG context, which is tangentially related to the SWA/flatness component of the RQ. However, it does not address CIFAR-C corruptions, SAM, CKA representation stability, or the SAM-vs-SWA comparison central to the RQ.
